a_restatement: An AI agent's "memory" is an architecture that extracts memory objects from user interactions, stores them in a datastore, and retrieves them by relevance when responding to queries.
Stored memories are corrected and consolidated when new input matches prior objects, and are deleted either on explicit request or automatically after a specified expiration time.
This system solves the problem of memoryless agents forgetting details, providing a described structural architecture rather than a marketing claim.

b_answers.answer: A model decides what to store by predicting what is worth remembering from cached inputs and extracting that information; one trigger for storage is explicit user request, such as asking the agent to remember something specific.
b_answers.quoted_span: A model decides what to store: cached inputs go to the model system, which predicts what is worth remembering and extracts it. It is stored as a memory value in a memory object, and one trigger is you asking the agent to remember your favorite architect.

b_answers.answer: It is stored as a memory value in a memory object.
b_answers.quoted_span: It is stored as a memory value in a memory object

b_answers.answer: It ranks stored objects by relevance to the query, comparing query embeddings to memory value embeddings using cosine similarity, keeps the top subset, and orders them by timestamp.
b_answers.quoted_span: At query time the agent does not reread everything; it ranks stored objects by relevance to your query. It compares a query embedding to memory value embeddings by a measure such as cosine similarity, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.

b_answers.answer: It queues the information for deletion to occur after that specified time period.
b_answers.quoted_span: "forget this after three months" queues it for deletion.

b_answers.answer: The prior memory object is replaced or updated; aligned objects can be consolidated into one, and a contradiction refines the matched memory rather than overcorrecting it.
b_answers.quoted_span: new timestamped input is matched to the prior memory object it concerns, which is then replaced or updated. Aligned objects can be consolidated into one, and a contradiction refines the matched memory rather than overcorrecting it.

b_answers.answer: The problem is that agents forget, requiring users to re-enter the same details repeatedly. The system's different approach is that it is a described architecture (not a marketing slogan) with structured features: memory objects made from user interactions, some stored on explicit request, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when requested.
b_answers.quoted_span: Agents forget, so you re-enter the same details; the claim is a loop — query plus memory data from a datastore of your past interactions, into a sequence model, out as a response.
